cohorts.summary: Reviewers highlight the interconnected level design and lack of fast travel, alongside slow animations and unclear paths.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks fast travel during the early and mid portions, making the interconnected level design stand out.

citations.review_text:
After Elden Ring, Dark Souls 3, Sekiro, and a little bit of Bloodborne, I was hesitant to try this game. But after a few hours in, I was blown away by how well the levels were designed.

In later FS games, there are some areas that feel boring (large and empty) or overly complicated. This is the opposite, and by far, it was the best experience I've had with a Souls game. Almost every area is connected due to not having fast travel, and all of them are filled with something to do (enemies, loots, NPCs, hard but fun puzzles, etc.).

The game is old, and some of its systems are outdated and rigid, but for a classic masterpiece, it is still a game that everyone should play and enjoy.

10/10

To be transparent, it took me a long time to get into DS1. Compared to titles like Elden Ring, DS3, and Sekiro, movement felt too slow and clunky, the world felt super confusing, and I felt lost all the time. However, one day it really clicked for me. As most others say, DS1's best trait is its level design and how every level is interconnected. Especially without fast travel in the early-mid game, you really come to appreciate the thought Fromsoft put into the design of the levels. Bosses are good generally, but defintely a tier below DS3 and Elden Ring, with a few exceptions that I won't spoil. Also, the DLC has some of my favourite bosses from the game so you should check it out if you get the game. Highly recommend!

To be entirely honest, this game has its place in history but it definitely shows its age in terms of feeling, control and enemy/world design.

There is definitely a first half of the game that feels decent to playthrough despite the clunkiness, but later on it eventually becomes a copy and paste hell and is unusually difficult.

Dark Souls 1 is a good game for what it is, but I cannot recommend it strongly as further installments are more enjoyable and superior to play.

Feels like a game from the early 2000s.

The healing is the slowest animation I've seen in my entire life, and you can't move while... drinking? Getting up after being hit down feels like my character is 200kg, this is one of the most clunkiest games I've ever played in my entire life... There are games released around the same time that are way better. I wanted to like DS1, but it seems everyone is talking from nostalgia.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the second half of the game, including areas like Lost Izalith, the Duke's Archives, and Lord Soul encounters, drops significantly in quality compared to the acclaimed first half.

citations.review_text: Absolute cinema, this game's first half is the definition of perfection. Then the second half starts and for your first playthrough it does the job, However in subsequent playthroughs it falls off dramatically if I had to rate the first half 10/10 the second half gets a 4/10 everything could have been improved and  I really hope that this game gets a remake that fixes the problems with the second half. ps Ds3 sucks.

Finishing my first ever playthrough of Dark Souls 1, I thought it was a good game. The world design is phenomenal. The atmosphere hits just right too! The first half of the game is just breathtaking and chef's kiss. 
Now what keeps me from saying this is a great game is primarily the Lord Souls in the second half of the game. The areas, the bosses, it felt like the quality that the first half of the game had lost its touch when doing each Lord Soul. But then the dlc hits, and it makes up for that loss of quality feel. Artorias was a phenomenal boss, Kalameet was my favorite dragon boss of the game, Manus felt like a great final boss for the dlc. Sif felt so much more impactful after doing the dlc, even making me cry with the boss fight. Then finally once all was done with dlc and Lord Souls, the journey of the Chosen Undead comes to an end and Gwyn, Lord of Cinder felt like a satisfying conclusion to the entire journey that led up to this very moment. 
I had fun with the game, it was challenging but it wasn't impossible and had me realize I should never downplay myself for nothing is impossible and you can do it no matter how hard it is. With patience, practice, calmness, and more you can conquer it all. This game is a journey that I feel people should experience at least once for it is a good game, a satisfying game. Remember, don't you dare go hollow.

Before picking this up, I used to say "I'm never playing a soulslike." Now, it’s the first game of the genre I’ve ever finished and I 100%ed it. Let's be real, with a game that hides this many secrets, you haven't truly beaten it until you get the Platinum. 3 playthroughs later and I still feel like I haven't seen everything.

The gameplay is simple but addictive. The interconnected world delivers a unique atmosphere a blend of coziness and eeriness that I hadn't felt since RDR1. The real difficulty lies in exploration and surviving the map because the bosses are on the slower side (makes sense for an older entry), but they fit the vibe perfectly.

The DLC is fantastic, Solaire and Siegmeyer are absolute legends, and my only real complaints are the overly cryptic lore (wished it was a bit more accessible) and the Duke's Archives / Lost Izalith (along with the Bed of Chaos) areas which felt like a chore. Surprisingly, Tomb of the Giants didn't bother me at all.

Even in 2026, Dark Souls Remastered stands tall as something fresh and revolutionary. It is the "The Sopranos" of video games. Praise the SUN! ☀️

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks early fast travel, requiring players to rely on walking and unlocking world interconnectivity until progressing to the second half.

citations.review_text: i want early fast travel :(

My first souls game being Elden Ring, coming to this game directly after was a completely different experience. Although it took a bit to get used to, with the clunkier movement, less bonfires, and fast travel limitations until the second half of the game, this is undoubtedly one of my favorite games of all time, for a plethora of reasons. 

The characters are amazing, following Solaire's and Siegmeyer's questlines made me genuinely emotional, as well as the overall story being nothing like anything I had ever experienced before, earning a permanent place in my heart as a world I will probably carry with me for the rest of my life. 

Coming from Elden Ring, the boss quality in this game is definitely worse on average, but the design and story of each boss makes up for their lacking gameplay, and almost all are memorable. The soundtrack that accompanies each boss is also amazing, with the soundtrack to the final boss being, in my opinion, the peak of gaming soundtracks, perfectly fitting the state of the Dark Souls world and the character it represents, begging you to break the cycle of fire.

The level design is probably the best of any game I have ever played, with each area feeling unique and memorable, (although there are a couple that kinda suck), and every level is interconnected with insane levels of detail and meticulous thought. 

If you have not played this game, I would highly recommend it, as it is downright lifechanging, as cringe as it is to say, but the ~60 hours I put into my first playthrough were worth every minute.

This was my first Souls game, and I would say it was well worth it. I had never played any difficult games before Dark Souls 1, and it prepared me for my journey ahead as a gamer to tackle even greater challenges. After Dark Souls 1, I went on to play every Souls game.
Talking about the game itself, it has some of the best level design you'll ever find. Everything connects with each other so well. You might not find the boss fights that challenging, but reaching each boss is a challenge on its own because the mobs will chase you all the way to the fog door, haha.The lore is amazing too, and interacting with the NPCs and getting to know them makes the journey even more special for me. It's a masterpiece, easily a 10/10.

Dark Souls.

Where it all started. Some of the boss runbacks in this game are quite literally atrocious, but the boss battles themselves are unforgettable.

Be prepared to be unrelenting attempting to beat this game, as with all dark souls games. In my opinion, it's so worth it if you can persevere. Praise the sun!

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the combat and movement feel clunky, slow, and sluggish, featuring long input buffering.

citations.review_text: this game sucks. its too clunky, the hitboxes are awful, the flask takes 40 minutes to drink, weapons suck, i can go on and on

One of the few "must play games" of all time. Dark Souls is a spectacular feat in almost every respect and one of the best games I've ever played. It's punishing, unforgiving, and intentionally confusing. It doesn't care if you get filtered by it. You'll just end up as one of the many hollows who bounced off of it. But if you keep pushing through and beat that next thing you got stuck on, it will feel amazing. The setting is that of a decaying, dark fantasy world. Everything is falling apart and there are barely any normal people left. They've all lost their minds - turned hollow. The game sets this vibe up amazingly with great level design, music, enemy design, and character design. The remaster does an amazing job of improving the presentation (same with DSfix).

I really enjoy the combat and general gameplay (with the exception of a few sections). It's slow and sluggish, inputs are stored for a ridiculously long time. But that all adds to the fun of the challenge and mastering those irritating controls. There's a lot of build variety, encouraging repeat playthroughs (even if some of said builds are very unbalanced).

The first souls-game you play will generally be your favorite and this is true for me. Dark Souls 1 is my favorite FromSoft souls-like I've played (have not played Elden Ring at the time of writing). That said, the game is not perfect - there are a few bugs in the remaster albeit usually minor. Still not nearly as bad as base Dark Souls 1 on PC though. Camera is god awful too.

If you are constantly getting filtered by the game, keep pushing and "git gud", once you overcome the first major obstacle, it will feel otherworldly, you'll seek that feeling of accomplishment again and again, feeling it everytime you surpass another obstacle

"And be safe, friend. Don't you dare go hollow..."

Dark Souls 1 definitely shows its age sometimes and can feel a little clunky compared to the newer games, but honestly that never stopped it from being amazing to me. Exploring Lordran for the first time is something I genuinely don’t think I’ll forget. It’s difficult, weird, lonely, and sometimes frustrating, but that’s also what makes it fun.

citations.review_text: this game is amazing but unfortunately you can't really play online without some person hacking and invading you. certain people will straight up not take damage and just backstab you from across the map. like i'm just trying to play games with my friends bro leave us alone, can't believe some people actually get enjoyment from hacking this game the way they do. great for single player though.

"Is dark souls good?" Is like asking if my wife would stop cheating on me. The answer is yes, if you are willing to forgive. The lore is simply poetry and the world is beautifully crafted. I bought this game for Xbox and steam so there seems to be a few differences but I feel like they are obvious. Looks better on pc, less cheaters on console. I wouldn't let cheaters ruin my experience though or deter the fact that I've bought the same game multiple times so hopefully it doesn't with others either. I've really only ran into one but other comments with more playtime make it seem more common than it is. Nonetheless, the characters they have are some of the best. Whether it means dying to save your best friend or being driven mad by a parasite while trying to shine some light on such a dark world. I just wish there was more cutscenes that explains it better because you have to search and pay attention otherwise you might not know that you offer the souls to Gwyn when you level up or other aspects of the lore. Captivating poetry that you can explore is the best way to describe the entire series and highly recommend for anyone trying to "Git Gud".  --BogDog

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Experienced players note the complete absence of hand-holding, guides, or tutorials, alongside input drops.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game drops controller inputs, particularly when attempting to use a shield during combat.

citations.review_text:
Changed my review to negative because it's simply unforgivable to leave in the action queueing and the bug where you get a staggered and then dodge without pressing anything.
In a game that is known for it's difficult combat and boss fights, this is simply inexcuseable. You really notice in fights that come down to: hitting all your dodges/attacks/etc perfectly.
It sucks, I love the game to death. Beat it 3 more times directly after my blind playthrough. But these devs are really taking us through the ringer these days. It's a lazy PC port, simple as that. DS2 is WAY worse in this regard, they did NOTHING beyond making sure the game runs, you can't even use keyboard/mouse on the PC version.

This is a fantastic game and I absolutely recommend everyone play this game. It's reputation is deserved but it's not unbeatable, with perseverance, determination and willpower anyone can get through this. Dark Souls Remaster does play slower and different from it's later counterparts especially the combat so I suggest taking things slow and getting comfortable with your preferred method of combat. It does not explain mechanics and expects you to either figure it out or look up how the mechanics work, items do explain what they do in their description so I suggest reading all the items you pick up to see if they'll be useful to you or not. When i started playing this game it would crash often and the way I fixed this was going into the Nvidia control panel and forcing its FPS to 55, this is an old game and doesn't like higher FPS. I also had to switch from controller to M&K halfway through my playthrough due to the game dropping inputs for me especially when I was trying to shield. I did research and apparently this is a problem for a good amount of players, I did try the controller on other games and it worked just fine so it was an input issue with the game. I would suggest committing to M&K from the start, it's really not that bad especially when you get the hang of it and to be honest I actually prefer it, or, testing your controller inputs thoroughly before committing because it was very annoying switching halfway through the game. To finish this review off, this is an amazing game and in my opinion well worth the money.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game contains no quest markers, quest logs, or hand-holding guidance, requiring players to pay attention to dialogue and the environment to navigate.

citations.review_text:
Dark Souls is what I'd describe as a truly unique and unforgettable experience. It never holds your hand. There are no quest markers or quest logs telling you exactly where to go or what to do. Instead, you're encouraged to pay attention to the world, the dialogue, and the characters around you. Everything feels organic, drawing you deeper into the world instead of constantly reminding you that you're playing a game.

If you're playing for the first time, I highly recommend playing online. The messages left by other players add so much charm to the experience, especially the helpful "Try jumping" messages.

The environmental storytelling is phenomenal, and even the difficulty of the bosses is woven into the narrative. Their strength reflects their history, their condition, and their place in the world. The world itself is masterfully designed, with every area seamlessly connecting in a way that makes exploration feel natural and rewarding.

It can be frustrating, punishing, and even rage-inducing at times, but that's exactly what makes overcoming its challenges so rewarding. The game doesn't teach you that you're bad at it; it teaches you patience, perseverance, and the value of learning from your mistakes. By the time you reach the end, you're left with a genuine sense of accomplishment that very few games outside of the Soulslike genre can replicate. Every step of the journey feels earned, and every victory feels like it truly belongs to you.

Don't go hollow out there. Persevere.

This game will at times be unfair and frustrating, making you feel despair, rage, and elation. It's not usually the style of game that I play or enjoy...but these are some of the reasons why it might be worth your time to play it.

1. The challenge. You can be level 100 and still get killed by the starting game enemies. This game will humble you and teach you to never take lightly any enemy great or small. You might have a boss down to 
1HP and think you can just phone it in and take him lightly...that's when you lose. You can't just level your way out of this game...you have to figure out the patterns, learn to dodge, block, parry, recharge stamina...there's a variety of ways you can play this game! All will require some skill!

2. No guidance. Tired of games holding your hand and telling you what to do? Tired of explicit storytelling? Want to actually have to listen to what people say and explore? You see that difficult jump? We'll it's not just a challenge but pretty much essential to a branch of the game. Sure, I'll admit that some of the secrets are absolutely impossible to find on your own. And that's fine. That's for New Game+. But you can absolutely beat this game without a walkthrough or tutorial. I did, and I recommend you do that same! It will be time consuming and you'll die a lot but you'll assuredly git gud.

3. It's a "souls" game. You ought to play at least one in this genre. I've heard Elden Ring is great but I'm glad I started with the OG.

I would suggest committing to M&K from the start, it's really not that bad especially when you get the hang of it and to be honest I actually prefer it, or, testing your controller inputs thoroughly before committing because it was very annoying switching halfway through the game. To finish this review off, this is an amazing game and in my opinion well worth the money.
